In [[functional analysis]], the '''Ciesielski's isomorphism''' establishes an [[isomorphism|isomorphism]] between the [[Banach space]] of [[Hölder condition|Hölder continuous]] functions <math>C^{\alpha}([0,T],\mathbb{R})</math>, equipped with a [[norm (mathematics)|norm]], and the space of [[sequence space|bounded sequences]] <math>\ell^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})</math>, equipped with the [[supremum norm]], by [[Schauder basis|coefficients of a Schauder basis]] along a sequence of dyadic partitions.

The statement was proved in 1960 by the Polish mathematician [[Zbigniew Ciesielski]].<ref>{{cite journal|first=Zbigniew |last=Ciesielski |title=On the isomorphisms of the spaces 𝐻𝛼 and 𝑚. |journal=Bull. Acad. Polon. Sci. Sér. Sci. Math. Astronom. Phys. |volume =8 |date=1960 |issn=0001-4117 |pages=217–222}}</ref> The result can be applied in [[probability theory]] when dealing with paths of the [[Brownian motion]].<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Paolo |last1=Baldi |first2=Bernard |last2=Roynette |title=Some exact equivalents for the Brownian motion in H{\"o}lder norm |journal=Probability Theory and Related Fields |volume=93 |date=1992 |pages=457-484 |url=https://api.semanticscholar.org/CorpusID:119685624}}</ref>

== Ciesielski's isomorphism ==
Let <math>[0,T]</math> be an intervall and let <math>\mathbb{T}=(\tau_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}</math> be a sequence of dyadic partitions of <math>[0,T]</math>.

Let <math>C^{\alpha}([0,T],\mathbb{R})</math> for <math>0<\alpha<1</math> be a Banach space of Hölder continuous functions with norm
:<math>\|f\|_{C^{\alpha}}=\|f\|_{\infty}+|f|_{C^{\alpha}}:=\sup\limits_{t\in [0,T]}|f(t)|+\sup\limits_{\begin{matrix}s,t\in[0,T]\\ s\neq t\end{matrix}}\frac{|f(s)-f(t)|}{|s-t|^{\alpha}}</math>
and <math>\ell^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})</math> be the Banach space of bounded sequence with [[supremum norm]]
:<math>\|a\|_{\infty}:=\sup\limits_{n}|a_n|</math>.

The map <math>S\colon C^{\alpha}([0,T],\mathbb{R})\to \ell^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})</math> defined as
:<math>f\mapsto \left(2^{(m+1)\left(\alpha-\tfrac{1}{2}\right)}|\theta(f)^{\mathbb{T}}_{m,k}| \right)_{m,k},\qquad (m,k)\in\mathbb{N}_0\times \{0,1,\dots,2^m-1\}</math>
is an [[isomorphism]], where <math>\theta(f)^{\mathbb{T}}_{m,k}</math> are the Schauder coefficients of <math>f</math> along <math>\mathbb{T}</math> of <math>[0,T]</math>.

The Schauder coefficients are
:<math>\theta(f)^{\mathbb{T}}_{m,k}=\langle f',h_{m,k} \rangle_{L^1}=\int_0^T f'(x)h_{m,k}(x)dx.</math>
for [[Haar wavelet|Haar functions]] <math>h_{m,k}</math> based on the dyadic partition <math>\tau_m</math>.

=== Properties ===
* The result was generalized in 2025 for general partitions.<ref>{{cite journal |first1=Erhan |last1=Bayraktar |first2=Purba |last2=Das |first3=Donghan |last3=Kim |title=Hölder regularity and roughness: Construction and examples |journal=Bernoulli |volume=31 |number=2 |date=2025 |pages=1084–1113 |doi=10.3150/24-BEJ1761|arxiv=2304.13794 }}</ref>
